title: Finca Son Ponent
description: Finca Son Ponent transforms a historic Mallorcan possessió into a private home rooted in the terraces of the Tramuntana. The original stone house retains its weight and domestic character, while a low contemporary extension is partially embedded into the landscape.
caption: Finca Son Ponent, Mallorca

title: Serrano Heights
description: Set at the highest point of Calle Serrano’s residential stretch, Serrano Heights transforms a historic Madrid building into a collection of contemporary residences, combining restoration of the original architecture with a restrained rooftop extension.
caption: Serrano Heights, Madrid

title: Alcalá Apartment I
description: A refined renovation of a historic Madrid apartment, where classical proportions are balanced with contemporary interventions, integrated joinery and a restrained palette of natural stone, dark timber and warm neutral finishes.
caption: Alcalá Apartment I, Madrid

title: CIFO
description: A private art archive and museum with an adjoining retail and commercial space, designed to house a permanent collection alongside exhibitions open to the public.
caption: CIFO, Miami

title: Casa Jungla
description: Conceived as a precise intervention within a steep tropical landscape, Casa Jungla follows the contours of the mountain through a sequence of long horizontal volumes. Deep concrete slabs, operable timber screens and shaded terraces mediate between domestic life and the surrounding rainforest.

title: Caledonian Road
description:
Developed for a private investor, the project explored the conversion of four adjoining London townhouses into a coordinated short-stay residential product.

The work established the overall spatial strategy, including access, ground-floor and basement extensions, additional mansard accommodation and the internal configuration of the individual units. The architectural proposal was developed alongside the interior concept, material palette and FF&E specification to create a consistent identity across the properties while retaining the scale and character of the existing buildings.
caption: Caledonian Road, London

title: Casa Riberas
location: Barrio Riberas, Puertos del Lago, Buenos Aires, Argentina
status: Design and Municipal Approval Package Completed · Construction by Client-Appointed Team
description:
Commission for a private residence developed from the initial project definition through municipal approval. The work included the overall architectural concept, spatial organisation, material strategy and preparation of the documentation required for approval.

Following completion of the design package, the clients appointed their own construction team and managed the delivery of the house independently.

The project was conceived as a contemporary family home organised around a strong relationship between interior spaces, garden and outdoor living areas. Large openings, protected terraces and layered façade elements balance openness with privacy, while a restrained material palette gives continuity to the different volumes.

The architecture combines clear horizontal planes with vertical timber elements, using changes in depth, transparency and material to articulate the elevations without relying on excessive formal gestures.

A complete architectural and municipal approval package was delivered to the clients, who subsequently appointed their own construction team to execute the project. Limited architectural support continued during construction when specific design clarifications or additional details were required.
caption: Casa Riberas, Puertos del Lago

title: El Naudir House
location: El Naudir, Puertos del Lago, Buenos Aires, Argentina
description:
Commission for a private residence within El Naudir, Puertos del Lago. The engagement began prior to the acquisition of the site, including plot assessment and selection, and continued through the development of the architectural concept and documentation required for licensing.

The project was developed around the relationship between the house, its lakefront setting and the internal landscape. The design establishes a sequence from a more controlled street frontage to increasingly open living spaces towards the garden and water, using double-height volumes, deep overhangs and large framed openings to strengthen the connection between interior and exterior.

A complete architectural and licensing package was delivered to the client, providing the basis for contractor selection and the subsequent construction phase.
caption: El Naudir House, Puertos del Lago

title: Bowas Soho
description:
Developed for Bowas as an urban residential product for Palermo Soho, the project combined market positioning, feasibility and architectural design. The strategy established a diverse unit mix, shared amenities and ground-floor commercial space around a contemporary live-work lifestyle.

The work extended from early product definition and architectural concept through interior design and planning documentation.
caption: Bowas Soho, Palermo Soho

title: Bowas Conesa
description:
Conceived as Bowas’ first residential development in Colegiales, the project translated the characteristics of a low-rise corner site into a distinct housing product. Feasibility and product studies informed the unit mix, layouts and relationship between private and shared outdoor space.

The architectural concept was developed alongside the interior design and planning documentation, with all residences oriented towards the street and larger units and communal amenities occupying the upper levels.
caption: Bowas Conesa, Colegiales

title: Maribor Country House
description:
Concept proposal for a private country house in a rural village outside Maribor, Slovenia. The project explored how a contemporary residence could sit naturally within a wooded, low-density landscape while retaining the directness and solidity associated with traditional rural architecture.

The house is conceived as a low, elongated volume organised beneath a simple pitched roof. Rather than treating the landscape as a backdrop, the plan and section are shaped around long views, sheltered outdoor spaces and a continuous relationship between the interior and the garden.

A restrained palette of light brick, timber and large glazed openings gives the building a quiet, monolithic character externally, while the interiors become warmer and more tactile through extensive timber surfaces and natural finishes.
caption: Maribor Country House, Slovenia

title: Belgrano House
description:
Renovation of an existing private residence in Belgrano, Buenos Aires, developed independently in collaboration with a local furniture studio. The commission formed part of an ongoing collaboration in which I developed the architectural and interior design of residential projects, while the studio contributed the furniture selection and supply.

The project reworked the existing house through a restrained contemporary language, balancing the character of the original building with a warmer and more precise interior atmosphere.

Externally, the intervention simplifies the composition through light rendered surfaces, timber elements and carefully framed openings, creating a quieter relationship with the mature tree-lined streets typical of Belgrano.

Internally, the renovation combines warm oak flooring, subtle wall mouldings, natural stone and controlled lighting. The intention was to create spaces that feel residential and layered rather than overly styled, allowing furniture and materiality to carry most of the visual character.

A complete renovation and interior design proposal was developed for the client, defining the architectural intervention, spatial character, material palette and key interior details, with furniture specified and supplied by the collaborating studio.
caption: Belgrano House, Buenos Aires
